::: {#thm-partial-f-null}
#### Null distribution of the partial F statistic

Let the errors of the [larger model](#def-nested-regression-models) be [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) and Gaussian
with mean $0$ and the same [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance).
If $H_0$ of @def-partial-f-test holds,
then $F$ has the $F_{q,\, n-p-1}$ distribution
for every number of observations $n > p + 1$.

Source: @vittinghoff2e [Section 4.3].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.proof}
Under $H_0$, $(\text{RSS}_0 - \text{RSS}_1) / \varpar$ has the $\chi^2_q$ distribution
and $\text{RSS}_1 / \varpar$ has the $\chi^2_{n-p-1}$ distribution,
where $\varpar$ is the error [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance).
The two are [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt),
because $\text{RSS}_1$ is the squared length of the part of the [outcome vector](model-validation.qmd#def-outcome-vector)
orthogonal to the [larger model](#def-nested-regression-models)'s [fitted values](prediction.qmd#def-fitted-value),
while $\text{RSS}_0 - \text{RSS}_1$ is the squared length of the part
in the larger model but orthogonal to the smaller one.
Dividing each by its degrees of freedom,
$\varpar$ cancels from the quotient, which is therefore $F_{q,\, n-p-1}$
by [the definition of the F-distribution](inference.qmd#def-f-dist).
:::
